title: Profile Input Value
prompt: A React profile controlled input must always receive a string. Write a helper that returns the provided value unless it is null, then returns an empty string.

explanation.beginner:
Example: profileInputValue("hello") produces "hello". Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Compare “converts null to empty string”: input [null] produces "". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Tempting mistake: A truthiness check also replaces 0, false, and an empty string. Nullish absence and falsiness are different rules.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “converts null to empty string”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
